full_text_en:
Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co., Ltd. v. United Parcel Service of America, Inc. — dispute over compensation for delayed express delivery of bid documents under international air cargo transport contract

Plaintiff: Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Liu Shaoyao, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agents ad litem: Yang Zhiao and Sun Jianming, lawyers of Shanghai Foreign Economic Law Firm.

Defendant: United Parcel Service of America, Inc. (hereinafter referred to as UPS), address: 55 Glenlake Parkway, NE, Atlanta, Georgia, United States.

Legal Representative: Robert Craning, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agents ad litem: Wang Xiaoyun, lawyer of New Century Law Firm; Chen Jianhua, Manager of Legal Department of Sinotrans Shanghai Company.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co., Ltd., brought an action before the Jing'an District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendant, United Parcel Service of America, Inc., concerning a dispute over compensation for delay in the express delivery of bid documents under an international air cargo transport contract.

**Plaintiff's Allegations**

The plaintiff, Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenhua Co., Ltd.), alleged that: In order to participate in the bidding for the quayside container crane project of the Port Authority of the Republic of Yemen, the plaintiff entrusted the defendant with the express delivery of bid documents on the morning of July 21, 1993, requesting that the documents be delivered to the designated location before the 25th of that month. The defendant indicated that it could deliver them on time. However, due to the negligence of the defendant's handling staff, the bid documents were detained in Shanghai for two days and only reached the designated location on the afternoon of July 27, 1993, after the bidding deadline of July 26, 1993, causing the plaintiff to lose the opportunity to bid and incur substantial economic losses and lost profits. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to refund the freight paid of RMB 1,432, compensate for direct economic losses of USD 10,360, and bear the litigation costs.

**Defendant's Defense**

The defendant, United Parcel Service of America, Inc., argued that: The defendant and the plaintiff had no clear agreement on the date of arrival of the bid documents at the destination; the defendant's express delivery of the bid documents for the plaintiff took six days and five hours, which did not exceed the reasonable transport time of four to seven days for international express items from China to Yemen, and there was no fact of delayed delivery. The two-day detention of the bid documents in Shanghai was due to the plaintiff's failure to specify the category and nature of the express item as required, which made it impossible for the defendant to go through customs clearance; the responsibility lies with the plaintiff. Even if the defendant was delayed in delivery and should compensate, compensation should be made in accordance with the maximum liability limit of the carrier provided in the Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules Relating to International Carriage by Air or the Protocol to Amend the Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules Relating to International Carriage by Air signed at Warsaw on 12 October 1929 (hereinafter referred to as the Warsaw Convention) and its amending Protocol (hereinafter referred to as the Amending Protocol). The plaintiff's claims have no legal basis and should be dismissed by the court.

**Facts Found by the Court**

The Jing'an District People's Court found through trial that: On the morning of July 20, 1993, the plaintiff, Zhenhua Co., Ltd., telephoned the defendant's UPS canvasser, indicating that it needed to send a document by express to the Republic of Yemen for bidding on July 21. In the afternoon of that day, the defendant gave the plaintiff a UPS waybill for the plaintiff to fill out. On the reverse side of the waybill, it was printed that "the Warsaw Convention and its amending Protocol are fully applicable to this waybill" and "the shipper agrees to the terms on the reverse side of this waybill and authorizes UPS to act as its export and customs clearance agent." On the morning of July 21, the defendant picked up the bid documents from the plaintiff and signed in the space for "UPS Receiving Representative Signature," indicating acceptance. After receiving the bid documents from the plaintiff, the defendant did not send them to Shanghai Hongqiao Airport for customs clearance on the same day. It was not until the evening of July 23 that the defendant completed the exit procedures for the bid documents. The bid documents arrived at the destination on July 27. Upon learning that the bid documents had not arrived at the destination before the bidding deadline of July 26, the plaintiff sent a letter to the defendant on July 27 requesting an investigation and response. The defendant replied, admitting that in handling the bid documents, UPS had committed three errors: (1) failing to strictly accept the items according to the receipt time (the cut-off time was 16:00, but the plaintiff's bid documents arrived at the defendant's Shanghai Pudong office at 16:45); (2) failing to carefully check the nature of the goods on the waybill; and (3) failing to ask the customer whether there were any additional requirements for time-sensitive delivery. The defendant expressed regret.

**Opinion of the Court**

The Jing'an District People's Court held that: The defendant, UPS, as a carrier, should have delivered the bid documents that the plaintiff, Zhenhua Co., Ltd., needed to send to the designated location promptly, timely, and safely. However, after accepting the bid documents on the morning of July 21, 1993, the defendant did not send them to the airport for customs clearance on the same day in accordance with industry practice, and did not clear and export the bid documents until the evening of July 23, causing the bid documents to be detained in Shanghai for two and a half days. The defendant's conduct violated the principle of prompt and timely express delivery and constituted a delay; it should bear corresponding civil liability. Although the plaintiff did not fill out the waybill in accordance with the requirements set forth in the defendant's waybill, after receiving the waybill filled out by the plaintiff, the defendant failed to carefully review it, and the responsibility lies with the defendant. The defendant's arguments that there was no fact of delayed delivery of the bid documents and that the main reason for the delayed export of the bid documents was the improper filling of the waybill by the plaintiff are untenable. The plaintiff's request for the defendant to refund the freight and compensate for direct economic losses lacks legal basis. Article 142, paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If an international treaty concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China contains provisions differing from those in the civil laws of the People's Republic of China, the provisions of the international treaty shall apply, unless the provisions are those on which the People's Republic of China has declared reservations." The Chinese government has both acceded to and ratified the Warsaw Convention and its amending Protocol. Article 11, paragraph 2 of the amending Protocol provides that: "In the carriage of registered baggage and cargo, the liability of the carrier is limited to a sum of 250 francs per kilogram, unless the passenger or consignor has made, at the time when the package was handed over to the carrier, a special declaration of interest in delivery at destination and has paid a supplementary sum if the case so requires." And it further provides: "If a part of the registered baggage or cargo, or any object contained therein, is lost, damaged, or delayed, the weight to be taken into consideration in determining the amount to which the carrier's liability is limited shall be only the total weight of the package or packages concerned." These provisions are clearly printed on the reverse side of the defendant's waybill, and therefore it should be deemed that both the plaintiff and the defendant have accepted the above provisions. The defendant shall compensate the plaintiff for economic losses in accordance with the maximum liability limit of the carrier as stipulated in the amending Protocol. The total weight of the bid documents as recorded on the waybill is 8 kilograms. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment on September 18, 1995:

1. The defendant, United Parcel Service of America, Inc., shall, within 10 days after the judgment takes effect, pay the plaintiff a lump-sum compensation of 2,000 francs (equivalent to RMB 12,695.47) for economic losses.

2. The plaintiff's other claims are dismissed.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed. The defendant has complied with the judgment.
